clinicalPearls: The most common of the three cerebral creatine deficiency syndromes and an important X-linked cause of intellectual disability in males.
X-linked (SLC6A8 on Xq28) defect of the creatine transporter; creatine synthesis is intact but creatine cannot be taken up into cells, notably neurons.

Affected males show intellectual disability, disproportionately impaired expressive speech and language, epilepsy, autistic and behavioural features and hypotonia; some have a movement disorder or gastrointestinal dysmotility.
Heterozygous carrier females may have learning difficulties and behavioural problems of variable severity owing to X-inactivation.
Biochemistry shows an elevated urinary creatine to creatinine ratio in affected males, with normal guanidinoacetate, helping separate it from the synthesis defects.
Brain proton MR spectroscopy shows a markedly reduced or absent creatine peak, as in the synthesis defects.

Crucially, it responds poorly to creatine supplementation because the transporter itself is defective; management is largely supportive, with creatine precursors such as arginine and glycine offering limited benefit.
Plasma creatine and guanidinoacetate may be normal, so a normal plasma screen does not exclude the diagnosis; the urinary ratio, spectroscopy and genetics are needed.
reference.pathophysiology: SLC6A8 (Xq28) encodes the sodium- and chloride-dependent creatine transporter that mediates cellular uptake of creatine, including transport across the blood-brain barrier and into neurons. Loss-of-function variants prevent creatine entering the brain despite normal endogenous synthesis and dietary intake, producing cerebral creatine depletion, impaired energy buffering and the resulting intellectual disability, speech impairment and epilepsy. Because the defect lies at the point of uptake rather than synthesis, exogenous creatine largely fails to reach the brain, which explains the poor response to supplementation that contrasts sharply with GAMT and AGAT deficiency. Inheritance is X-linked, so males are predominantly and more severely affected, while carrier females are variably affected through skewed X-inactivation. Creatine that cannot be taken into cells is excreted, giving the characteristic raised urinary creatine to creatinine ratio.
additionalDifferentials: GAMT and AGAT deficiency, the treatable creatine synthesis defects, which must be excluded
Fragile X syndrome and other X-linked intellectual disability disorders
Autism spectrum disorder and non-syndromic intellectual disability
Angelman syndrome (absent speech, seizures, behavioural phenotype)
additionalInvestigations: Urinary creatine to creatinine ratio (raised in affected males)
Plasma guanidinoacetate and creatine (often normal and not exclusionary)
Brain proton MR spectroscopy (reduced or absent creatine peak)
Molecular genetic testing of SLC6A8, with maternal carrier testing
Creatine uptake studies in cultured fibroblasts
redFlags: X-linked pattern of intellectual disability with disproportionate expressive speech impairment
A normal plasma metabolic screen giving false reassurance
Seizures with developmental delay or regression
reference.prognosis: Prognosis is guarded; unlike the synthesis defects it responds poorly to creatine, and most affected males have persistent intellectual disability, although many remain medically stable with supportive care.
pitfalls: Relying on normal plasma creatine or guanidinoacetate to exclude the diagnosis; the urinary ratio, spectroscopy and genetics are required.
The urinary ratio can be unreliable or normal in carrier females, so genetic testing is needed for carrier detection.
Expecting a creatine-supplementation response comparable to the synthesis defects.
Overlooking maternal carrier status and the X-linked recurrence risk.
references: Cerebral creatine deficiency syndrome consensus guidance
management: Offer a supervised trial of oral creatine monohydrate combined with the precursors L-arginine and glycine, while counselling that brain uptake is defective so response is typically poor unlike the synthesis defects
Control seizures with appropriate antiepileptic drugs guided by EEG and seizure type
Provide intensive developmental support with speech and language therapy targeting expressive communication, plus occupational therapy and physiotherapy for hypotonia and motor delay
Manage autistic and behavioural features with structured behavioural interventions and address gastrointestinal dysmotility symptomatically
Monitor with periodic EEG, developmental and educational review, and audiological and growth surveillance
Coordinate care through a metabolic medicine, neurology and developmental paediatric multidisciplinary team
Provide genetic counselling for this X-linked SLC6A8 disorder, offer maternal carrier testing, and screen at-risk female relatives who may have variable learning difficulties
